[[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

It is the central shrine of the Shiraiwa district, which roughly corresponds to the former {{ill|Shimoōmi|ja|下大見村|ko|시모오미촌|qid=Q11360758}}<ref name="tennen">[http://www.city.izu.shizuoka.jp/gyousei/gyousei_detail000109.html City-Designated Natural Monument] - Izu City</ref>.

== Overview ==
Many old {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}} (ridge plaques) are preserved, the oldest of which is inscribed with the 3rd year of {{ill|Kōan (Kamakura period)|Q389180|qid=Q389180}} (1280) in the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}<ref name="tennen"/><ref name="yuisho">Shrine grounds history inscription</ref>.

Because the nearby {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamishiraiwa Site}} dates back to the {{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}}, and because there is also a place name “Motomura” in the area, it is considered the oldest shrine established earliest in the surrounding region<ref name="tennen"/><ref name="yuisho"/>.

Before the Edo period, it was called '''Shiraiwa Ōasa Shrine''' (しらいわ おおあさじんじゃ), and together with {{ill|Yohara Shrine|Q11541065|qid=Q11541065|lt=Ōasa Shrine}} in Shimo Kanuki, {{ill|Numazu|Q241037|qid=Q241037}}, it is listed as a candidate for “Ōasa Shrine” in the {{ill|List of Shikinaisha in Izu Province|ja|伊豆国の式内社一覧|qid=Q11380552|lt=Shikinaisha}}<ref name="yuisho"/>. (In the nearby southeastern district (Yahata district), there is also {{ill|Kinomiya Shrine (Q119929624)|Q119929624|qid=Q119929624|lt=Kinomiya Shrine}}, which is a candidate for another Shikinaisha, “Sugihokowake-no-Mikoto Shrine.”)

The {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine forest}} surrounding the shrine buildings is designated as a city natural monument<ref name="tennen"/>.
